changes: Three scheduled personality review implementations become one registered handler flow, preserving the three schedule IDs, cron expressions, windows, token/topic limits, labels and memory metadata.
Personal memories are scoped once per user and reused for the period, fact and preference counts; organization and avatar exclusions are retained.

Seven standard OpenAI-compatible SDK getters share per-provider client and configuration-signature caching. Environment/stored key precedence, endpoint defaults, key removal and constructor failure behavior are preserved.
Official relay retry/error normalization, local private transports, provider routing and the Anthropic/Gemini clients are unchanged.

parity.method: Original and current production code with synthetic dependencies; no live credentials, network, or user database.

tests.replacementReason: The single OpenAI hot-reconfiguration case is retained and expanded to seven parameterized provider cases, including reuse and endpoint switching. Three review behavior cases were added.

generatedCallsiteChecks.reason: Three review model call sites were merged into one, so the unchanged AST-driven arity suite discovers two fewer sites; line-number labels also move. Every review still verifies all twelve provider getter arguments in behavior tests.

intentionalRetention: Customer and ecommerce contracts have similar object shapes but different required evidence, permitted tools and success criteria; they were reviewed and left separate.
Independent bundled skill extractors retain their installation and packaging boundary as documented in prune36.
limitations: Parity uses synthetic constructors, time, models and database collaborators; it is not live official-API or client acceptance.
The initial parity harness confused absent and undefined object fields and compared cross-VM prototypes; corrected the harness, not product behavior, before the recorded successful run.
No real response-latency improvement was measured.
Other approximate-duplicate candidates, including first-launch local-model detection, still require behavior and lifecycle review.
